text:
sarah: paging — hosted-us-east showing large request spike, p95 ~12s, p99 ~58s, queue backlog ~45k and growing. customers timing out. seeing GPU pool saturation across two clusters. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2234 — hosted-us-east queue growth / autoscaler errors. Severity: P1. Pager duty: @mike oncall.
ops-bot: cluster-metrics snapshot: us-east-1-gpu-pool-1 cpu: 92% | gpu-util: 99% | queue: 27000 -> us-east-1-gpu-pool-2 gpu-util: 100% | queue: 18000 | pending-pods: 0.
mike: on it. initial suspicion: autoscaler failed to bring new GPU nodes, maybe quota or cloud-side throttling. grabbing autoscaler logs now.
cheng: I see the same — autoscaler error: "FailedCreateInstances: quota exceeded for GPU type nvidia-a100" in cloud provider responses. repeated backoff.
emily: Support is getting inbound p95 complaints from 3 customers in the next hour. Olivia from CS standing by to coordinate comms.
mike: running `redwoodctl autoscaler status --cluster us-east-1` -> shows desired_replicas 60, active_replicas 40, scale_errors: ["QuotaExceeded", "LimitRangeExceeded"].
ops-bot: autoscaler log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:45Z scale loop: desired=60 actual=40 -> request create 20 instances
2026-03-15T03:12:46Z cloud API 403 QuotaExceeded: Request would exceed GPU quota for project
2026-03-15T03:12:46Z backoff: 1s -> 2s -> 4s
2026-03-15T03:13:02Z scale loop aborted: cloud create failed
```
cheng: there's also a scale limit set in infra-config: `max_gpu_per_cluster: 44` which is lower than the desired 60. That config should not be blocking but it is enforced by the orchestration layer. Looks like someone updated that during last change.
olivia: I'll draft a quick outbound to affected customers: "We're experiencing elevated latencies on hosted-us-east and are actively scaling capacity. We'll share ETA in 30 mins."
sarah: mitigation options: 1) emergency cloud quota bump (+50 GPUs) via cloud account (takes 10-30m) 2) disable the max_gpu_per_cluster guard to allow autoscaler to scale to desired 60 (fast) 3) enable cross-region routing to us-west for heavy requests (fast but may cause higher latency) 4) temporary rate-limit heavy API keys / throttle top hitters (immediate) 5) fallback to smaller model variants for non-enterprise customers (immediate but affects quality).
mike: I'm going to disable the `max_gpu_per_cluster` guard in infra-config and trigger a manual scale. Doing it now: `infractl update-config --cluster us-east-1 --set max_gpu_per_cluster=0`
mike: applied. triggering manual scale to 60: `redwoodctl scale cluster us-east-1 --gpus 60`
ops-bot: manual scale triggered. cloud responses still show QuotaExceeded for 20 instances. 40 instances are healthy.
cheng: because cloud quota is still blocking, manual scale won't fully resolve. pushing cloud quota request now — opened ticket #CLOUD-9091 with provider, asked for emergency quota increase. ETA unknown.
emily: Support: start throttling top keys. How many keys are responsible for the surge?
mike: run `redis-cli --bigkeys` -> top 10 API keys account for ~62% of current RPS. I'll cut them to 50% for hosted tier: applying rate limit rule now.
mike: `edgectl rate-limit add --key-file top-10-keys.csv --rate 50% --duration 30m` -> applied.
ops-bot: immediate effect: incoming RPS dropped 48%, queue growth slowed to +2k per minute. p95 improved from 12s -> 7s in 6 minutes.
olivia: Customer success update: notified top-5 customers, offering to route critical traffic to dedicated plan or to us-west. Two customers asked for ETA and were satisfied with temporary throttles.
emily: we should enable fallback model routing for public tier to move non-critical requests to smaller models: `routingctl set-fallback --from model/70b --to model/13b --percent 40`
cheng: rolled out fallback for non-enterprise = 40% traffic. logs show immediate drop in per-token GPU cost and slight drop in latency.
mike: also enabling soft-queue-shed: `frontendctl shed --backlog-threshold 30000 --drop-minority 20%` to keep head latencies for critical customers.
sarah: good. start timeline for incident report. capture key metrics: peak backlog 45k, peak p99 58s, affected customers: 14 with >5% error increase, mitigation steps: throttles, fallback models, manual infra config change, cloud quota requested.
incident-bot: Runbook: create postmortem doc link: /incidents/2234/postmortem (placeholder).
olivia: CS to send follow-up once we have ETA on cloud ticket.
mike: cloud provider responded: acknowledged, emergency review started; provisional +30 GPUs within 20-25 minutes.
ops-bot: once quota arrives autoscaler should provision remaining instances; we will monitor for any delayed failures.
cheng: temporary fix: I've queued a patch to infra-config to set sensible default `max_gpu_per_cluster: 200` and added a guard so config changes require a two-person approval. PR: `git+repo#fix/max-gpu-limit` -> merging after CI.
emily: handoff plan: I'm taking the next hour then handing to @cheng for overnight. include runbook steps and current mitigations.
sarah: oncall handoff notes: state = mitigation active, throttles in place, fallback at 40% for non-enterprise, cloud quota requested +30, desired_final_replicas=60, current=40. Pager duty: next oncall @cheng.
mike: leaving now, monitoring cloud ticket. If quota not granted in 25m we'll escalate to provider support lead and consider placing emergency reserved capacity from dedicated pool.
cheng: acknowledged. will watch overnight and coordinate draining backlog. leaving note to oncall: check `redwoodctl queue stats --cluster us-east-1` every 10m and `infractl events` for failed creates.
olivia: CS will log all customer-facing comms in the incident doc and follow up with impacted customers tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigations in place; severity downgraded to P2 at 03:52 UTC as latency and queue growth stabilized.
sarah: closing thread for active paging. continue monitoring; create postmortem draft tomorrow. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
